issues.title: Substring prefilter over contiguous string runs for LIKE/contains scan filters
issues.hypothesis: In q13 (648ms, 14.5% of the total) the orders TABLE_SCAN with the filter o_comment NOT LIKE '%unusual%packages%' takes 2.60s of CPU, the largest single operator in the profile. The join and the aggregate above it are now cheap after E0003. The ExpressionFilter is evaluated per row through the generic LIKE matcher. FSST decode with enable_fsst_vectors=false writes the strings back to back into one buffer, so a whole run of rows can be checked for the literal with one SIMD search. A previous run measured q13 -11% with this mechanism.
issues.plan: In src/storage/table/column_data.cpp, ColumnData::Filter (line 348): after Scan, if the filter is an EXPRESSION_FILTER whose expression is ~~ / !~~ / contains (or NOT of these) with a constant pattern that uses only '%' wildcards (no '_' or escape), extract the longest literal segment of at least 2 bytes. For a FLAT VARCHAR result, walk the rows and group the non-inlined strings whose data pointer equals the previous string's end into runs. Search each run with an SSE2 first+last-byte candidate scan and memcmp to confirm. Keep the scan block overlapping into the run tail; do not finish the tail with a scalar loop, because the prior run found that removes the gain. Map each hit back to its row (a hit must lie fully inside one string). Rows without the literal are decided directly: false for positive LIKE, true for NOT LIKE. Only candidate rows go through the original ColumnSegment::FilterSelection / expression, with a reduced selection. Inlined (<=12 byte) strings and non-contiguous strings fall back to the per-row path. Do not depend on FSST_VECTOR: it never reaches this path.
issues.expected_gain: q13 -10% (prior run -11%). Smaller gains for any other LIKE/contains scan filter (q09 p_name LIKE '%ghost%' on part, a small table).
issues.generality: Any substring-style LIKE/contains/NOT LIKE scan filter on VARCHAR columns, which are common in analytics (comments, names). Columns with short inlined strings fall back and so do not slow down. If almost every row matches the literal (no pruning), the extra pass adds a small overhead.
issues.risk: Medium. Correctness depends on NOT semantics, NULL handling (NULL rows must still be filtered out) and matches that cross a string boundary. The implementer should check results with dbe-tool sql against an equivalent filter that blocks pushdown (e.g. concat(o_comment,'') NOT LIKE ...).

issues.title: Join key-set range filter through compress projections
issues.hypothesis: q18 (695ms, 15.5%) scans all 59,986,052 lineitem rows for the l_orderkey = o_orderkey join, while only 111 orderkeys survive the HAVING semi join. The join filter pushdown cannot pass through __internal_compress_integral projections, and a single min/max range over random keys prunes nothing. A prior run (offset-aware pushdown plus an OptionalFilter OR of up to threshold ranges split at the largest gaps) measured q18 -13.6%, with lineitem scan rows going 60M→17.5M.
issues.plan: In src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp, follow column bindings through compress-integral projections and record the storage offset in JoinFilterPushdownColumn. In src/execution/operator/join/join_filter_pushdown.cpp (and wherever the min/max filters are built in physical_hash_join.cpp), when the build has few distinct keys (threshold < n <= 64*threshold), build an OptionalFilter holding an OR of ranges split at the largest gaps, with the offset added.
issues.generality: Selective joins against large fact tables whose keys are clustered by row group, and pushdown through compressed materialization in general.
issues.risk: Medium. Offsets must be applied correctly, but the filters are optional (zonemap only), so a wrong pruning decision is the main risk.

issues.title: Bloom filter on first key of multi-key hash joins
issues.hypothesis: In q09 (799ms, the largest template) the lineitem-partsupp join has 2 keys (ps_suppkey, ps_partkey). CanUseBloomFilter requires conditions.size()==1, so this join gets no BF. A prior run measured q09 -21% by building the BF on key 0 only.
issues.plan: In src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp InsertHashes, gather join key column 0 and hash it on its own for the BF. In physical_hash_join.cpp CanUseBloomFilter / FinalizeFilters, allow multiple conditions and push the BF only for the filter on join_condition 0.
issues.risk: Medium. The BF hash has to match the probe-side hashing.

output.memory:
## Memory (gen1)

## State
- r1: E0001 JoinDependentFilterRule before DistributivityRule ACCEPTED: q19 -46%, geomean -4.2%.
- r2: E0002 contains()/LIKE length-aware selectivity ACCEPTED: q09 -37%, geomean -3.9%.
- r3: E0003 Perfect HJ RIGHT v2 ACCEPTED: q13 -18..-20%. Best 1.091x. Large range (up to 4M) allowed only for RIGHT joins; for INNER it regressed q14 +52% and q18 +13% (serial perfect build, no BF).
- r4 DISPATCHED: substring prefilter over contiguous string runs (ColumnData::Filter, column_data.cpp:348). Target: q13 orders scan, 2.60s CPU.
- Current top templates: q09 799ms (17.9%), q18 695, q13 648, q04 310, q05 282.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run on this same codebase/workload. Treat them as strong measured priors, not as already-landed code. Read the specific memory .md files directly with Read.

## Prior-run wins to port, in rough priority order (gain / risk)
1-3. DONE (rule reorder, contains selectivity, perfect HJ RIGHT).
4. r4: substring prefilter (q13 -11%). Then FSST batched decode (q13 -4..-7%, gain only via DecompressVector).
5. Backlog: join key-set range filter through compress projs (q18 -13.6%). Semi-join RHS-aware estimate (q18 -8%).
6. Backlog: BF on first key of a multi-key HJ (q09 -21%). Then join filter through CM compress (q09 -8%), exact bitmap BF for dense int keys (q09/q16/q21 -10..-15%).
7. Large perfect HA (22-bit) + parallel source: q13 -18.6%. Distinct HT partitioned on group hash: q16 -12%.
8. OR-of-ranges as ExpressionFilter, dense mask eval: q19 -7..-11%.
9. Follow-up from E0003: parallel perfect HJ build, or keep the BF alongside it, which would unlock large-range INNER perfect HJ.
- q04 (310ms) has no prior idea; profile it once the ports run out.

## Known dead ends (prior run)
- HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ, bitpacking select: all ~0%.

## Codebase facts
- Rule registration order lives in src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp.
- Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter (relation_statistics_helper.cpp) has an EXPRESSION_FILTER case for contains/like.
- ColumnData::Filter = Scan + ColumnSegment::FilterSelection. enable_fsst_vectors defaults to false, so the filter sees flat decoded strings.
- Perfect HJ gates: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin; join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp computes min/max aggregates.
- Profile q18: lineitem scan 60M rows with no pruning. q13: orders scan with NOT LIKE takes 2.60s CPU.
- q04/q08 show ±7-12% bench noise; ignore single-run moves.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory/ledger, then dispatch the next prior win quickly.
